articles.title: Feature flags in WordPress plugins and Laravel apps without a vendor
articles.excerpt: Feature flags let you ship code before you ship the feature, but most teams either skip them or buy a platform they barely use. Here is how I build small, honest flags in WordPress plugins and Laravel apps, and how I keep them from rotting.

articles.title: Migrating a large WooCommerce store without losing orders
articles.excerpt: Store migrations rarely lose the catalog. They lose the orders and payments that land while the old and new servers both look live. Here is the cutover plan and reconciliation I use so every order ends up in one place.

articles.title: RAG over your own docs: a small, honest architecture
articles.excerpt: Most chat-with-your-docs projects fail on retrieval, not on the model: the right paragraph never reaches the prompt. Here is the small RAG architecture I build, with Postgres, citations, a refusal path and an eval set.

articles.title: Typed REST clients in TypeScript for WordPress and Laravel APIs
articles.excerpt: When a React app talks to a WordPress or Laravel API through scattered fetch calls, a renamed field breaks screens silently. Here is how I build one typed client per API so drift fails loudly in development, not quietly in production.

articles.title: Kubernetes for a small PHP team: when a single VPS is the better call
articles.excerpt: Kubernetes solves real problems, but a three-person PHP team often buys them a year early. Here is how I decide between one well-run VPS, a few boxes, and a cluster, and what has to be true before Kubernetes pays for itself.

articles.title: The first week on a legacy WordPress codebase: my audit routine
articles.excerpt: Inheriting a WordPress site nobody fully understands is risky in the first week, because every change is a guess. Here is the audit routine I run before touching code, so the first fix is safe and the plan is based on facts.

articles.title: Subscription billing edge cases: proration, failed renewals, dunning

articles.title: Laravel Octane in production: what changes and what breaks

articles.title: Estimating engineering work honestly: ranges, risks and what I tell clients

articles.title: WordPress multisite in 2026: when it still makes sense

articles.title: Shopify app or WooCommerce plugin: where to build a commerce product

articles.title: Adding AI features to a SaaS without a surprise API bill
